stage: parent and peer review; no additional rule relocation in this stage
basis: TAXONOMY.md philosophy and placement procedure, with the user instruction removing all directory-size waivers.
implemented: Uniform maximum of 100 atomic plus composite rules in every directory.
Updated validator messages, policy and regression tests.

decisions.metadata: Classify the asserted property, declaration, provenance or measurement. Subject names must add meaning independent of carrier.
decisions.metadata/file: Review as a redundant grouping candidate, not an accepted starting point. Whole-file measurement is a real observation scope, but that does not require a universal file container in its taxonomy path.
decisions.metadata/package: Retain distributed-component subjects; package is not a synonym for manifest.
decisions.metadata/package/dependencies/manifest: Remove as a level where it adds only the evidence carrier. Preserve declared/resolved/shipped distinctions where they alter the claim.
decisions.limits: A limit violation starts semantic review; it cannot choose the partition, justify an exception, or justify loss of a broad observation.

objectives/exfiltration/stealer/credenti.question: What authentication material is required to leave the endpoint?
objectives/exfiltration/stealer/credenti.parent_problem: The meaningful credential ancestor holds broad form-unknown theft claims alongside narrower password/token/key/record children. Source, transport and language cannot choose an item subtype.
objectives/exfiltration/stealer/credenti.disposition: Re-review all broad rules for required export, selected values versus whole files/records, and duplication of existing theft predicates. Factor repeated mechanics into canonical observations and consolidate equivalent result claims. A subtype move needs evidence for every passing alternative; unresolved broad claims remain explicit review holds.
objectives/exfiltration/stealer/credenti.counterexample: An API key and a password admitted as alternatives do not establish credential/token. A complete configuration file does not become a selected credential because it may contain one.
objectives/exfiltration/stealer/credenti.status: parent review complete; per-rule destination map pending

metadata/file/archive.question: Which property of the analyzed archive or its member table is observed?
metadata/file/archive.parent_problem: The file parent mixes whole-byte properties, names, archive structure, source properties and residual catalogs. Archive facts also overlap package/files/archive-member; the carrier does not create a second observation.
metadata/file/archive.disposition: Review archive observations together with package member facts, format signatures, signing and own-filename properties. Establish one subject home per fact. Determine whether a remaining archive catalog needs genuine member/layout/compression distinctions only after these relocations.
metadata/file/archive.counterexample: The scanned archive basename is an input-name fact. A member named certificate.RSA is a member-name fact, not a validated signature.
metadata/file/archive.status: parent review complete; per-rule destination map pending

micro-behaviors/communications/http/url/.question: What property of an HTTP URL path is required?
micro-behaviors/communications/http/url/.parent_problem: Peers mix URL components (host, path, query), services (github, cloud, registry), resource roles (script, media) and source expression forms (encoded, markup). api-path competes directly with path.
micro-behaviors/communications/http/url/.disposition: Review all URL peers on the component axis and compare protocol-neutral URL subjects. Route literals belong with path structure; service identity and dynamic construction are separate claims. Consolidate equivalent endpoint references before any path subdivision.
micro-behaviors/communications/http/url/.counterexample: /api/messages is a path reference, not an HTTP operation; a source expression constructing a URL is not another kind of path.
micro-behaviors/communications/http/url/.status: parent review complete; per-rule destination map pending

metadata/package/dependencies/manifest/i.question: Which dependency is identified by the required evidence?
metadata/package/dependencies/manifest/i.parent_problem: Dependency children mix evidence carriers (manifest, lockfile, archive), declaration origin, direct-URL sources and property facets. The archive directory even includes an npm dependencies.archiver declaration, demonstrating axis drift.
metadata/package/dependencies/manifest/i.disposition: Review every dependency branch against property facets: identity, name form, source, range, count, presence and reconciliation. Remove manifest where it only adds carrier information. Preserve whether a fact is requested, resolved or shipped in the claim and scope. Inventory named declarations against existing producer facts before retaining one YAML definition per dependency name; preserve stronger feature/section predicates separately.
metadata/package/dependencies/manifest/i.counterexample: A declaration requesting lodash, an installed lodash member and code importing lodash are different observations; none identifies the analyzed artifact as Lodash.
metadata/package/dependencies/manifest/i.status: parent review complete; per-rule destination map pending

metadata/file/naming.question: Which property of the analyzed input name or location is required?
metadata/file/naming.parent_problem: The file parent adds little to naming and shares its level with content subjects. naming combines basename content/shape, stem measurements and directory relationships; extension peers also contain filename properties.
metadata/file/naming.disposition: Review naming together with extension and package-member naming. Candidate subject homes are metadata/filename for the analyzed basename/stem and metadata/path for its containing location or multi-component relationships. Give member-table names an archive subject. Classify the complete population before selecting children within either name subject.
metadata/file/naming.counterexample: A directory named capiumbrowser is an input-location fact, not product identity. Code mentioning /tmp/cache is a path reference, not a property of the analyzed input name.
metadata/file/naming.status: parent review complete; per-rule destination map pending

micro-behaviors/communications/http/requ.question: Which request-payload operation or property is required?
micro-behaviors/communications/http/requ.parent_problem: request siblings mix content (json, credentials), verbs (get), carriers (query/body), platforms (wordpress), client libraries (httpx) and evidence forms (computed/reference). http/body, form and upload supply competing homes.
micro-behaviors/communications/http/requ.disposition: Review the request parent and HTTP peers as one boundary problem. Separate payload construction/content, sending a request, attachment upload and local source acquisition. Preserve established data relationships without classifying by client API or containing language.
micro-behaviors/communications/http/requ.counterexample: Base64 beside POST does not bind the encoded bytes to a body; a body-bearing POST does not establish file upload.
micro-behaviors/communications/http/requ.status: parent review complete; per-rule destination map pending

micro-behaviors/data/decode/base64.question: Does required evidence establish a Base64 decoding operation?
micro-behaviors/data/decode/base64.parent_problem: decode peers mix algorithms with input origin (environment/native/reflection Base64), carriers and repeated-transform mechanisms. JSON/source proximity observations can exceed their claimed decode relationship.
micro-behaviors/data/decode/base64.disposition: Apply direction/scheme admission to the complete population. Move scheme presence, imports and source syntax to their proper subjects; merge equivalent decoder observations across implementation scopes. Preserve required repeated decoding as a separate result. Do not split one Base64 operation merely by its input source.
micro-behaviors/data/decode/base64.counterexample: An alphabet or encoded blob is not decoding; importing a library with both directions does not establish decode.
micro-behaviors/data/decode/base64.status: parent review complete; per-rule destination map pending

micro-behaviors/fs/path/credential.question: What kind of resource does the referenced path point to?
micro-behaviors/fs/path/credential.parent_problem: Path peers mix resource (private-key, cookie, token), ownership (application), lexical evidence (basename, filename-credential), operations (construct/check) and broad locations.
micro-behaviors/fs/path/credential.disposition: Apply the credential resource precedence across the parent, checking every path against password-store, cookie, key, token, secret-config and ordinary configuration subjects. Move path operations and observations about the scanned input name out of resource references. Broad cross-form references must not acquire a guessed secret subtype.
micro-behaviors/fs/path/credential.counterexample: Reading no bytes from a referenced auth.json does not establish credential collection; a configuration file is not a private-key value.
micro-behaviors/fs/path/credential.status: parent review complete; per-rule destination map pending

micro-behaviors/communications/http/uplo.question: Does the required evidence establish a file or attachment send?
micro-behaviors/communications/http/uplo.parent_problem: HTTP peers mix methods, artifact transfer, client backends, endpoints and request source. This leaf includes multipart prefixes, file-backed curl options and HTTP-client/archive co-occurrences with different admission strength.
micro-behaviors/communications/http/uplo.disposition: Review upload alongside post, body, form, curl and client. Keep admitted attachment transfer; put request options, client references and co-occurrence at their supported subjects. Preserve scope and independently test any corrections to the upload claim.
micro-behaviors/communications/http/uplo.counterexample: A torrent archive containing an HTTP client does not show upload; POST alone is a request method.
micro-behaviors/communications/http/uplo.status: parent review complete; per-rule destination map pending

micro-behaviors/communications/http/head.question: Which meaning or operation of an HTTP header is required?
micro-behaviors/communications/http/head.parent_problem: custom is a residual naming class beside content, security, proxy, value and setting-operation peers. Several custom token headers have authentication meaning; forwarded-host is proxy provenance.
micro-behaviors/communications/http/head.disposition: Review the parent on header semantics. Authentication, content and forwarding evidence should use their canonical subjects. Keep a header observation neutral and explicit where the name does not establish a narrower meaning; assess duplication across http/auth, authorization-header and token-auth before adding children.
micro-behaviors/communications/http/head.counterexample: A service-specific token field is not generic simply because its name starts X-. A field name alone does not establish that a request set it.
micro-behaviors/communications/http/head.status: parent review complete; per-rule destination map pending

micro-behaviors/communications/http/post.question: Is a POST operation required, and is it the result the rule actually establishes?
micro-behaviors/communications/http/post.parent_problem: POST competes with request/client, request/body and upload for API observations, while some composites select credential content or combine local preparation with sending.
micro-behaviors/communications/http/post.disposition: Compare all method and payload peers. Keep method observations in post; route proven source-to-send theft by exported item, and retain independent content or staging facts at their subjects. Consolidate equivalent POST calls only after scope and binding comparison.
micro-behaviors/communications/http/post.counterexample: An encoded mnemonic selected and transmitted is a credential export claim; an axios.post call alone is neutral HTTP.
micro-behaviors/communications/http/post.status: parent review complete; per-rule destination map pending

micro-behaviors/fs/file/copy.question: Does the rule require a filesystem copy, and what copying result is observed?
micro-behaviors/fs/file/copy.parent_problem: fs/file peers mix operations (copy/move/open), resource kinds (binary/executable), argument roles and platforms. The higher fs level separately begins with operations such as read/write, so resource and operation axes are inconsistent.
micro-behaviors/fs/file/copy.disposition: Review copy against fs read/write and their resource refinements. Separate file copying from a read/write loop, deployment or packaging relationship, and API/path co-occurrence. Resolve the parent operation/resource axis before selecting a new level for copy.
micro-behaviors/fs/file/copy.counterexample: Reading lines and writing lines is not automatically a file copy unless the content relationship is established.
micro-behaviors/fs/file/copy.status: parent review complete; per-rule destination map pending

micro-behaviors/fs/write/file/full.question: Does the required evidence establish a whole-file write rather than another write operation or property?
micro-behaviors/fs/write/file/full.parent_problem: Peers mix mode (append/full), interface (descriptor/handle/stream), transport source (response-body), target kinds and attacker intent (webshell/masquerade). The same write can satisfy several siblings.
micro-behaviors/fs/write/file/full.disposition: Review the complete write parent and select one refinement axis with a tie-breaker. Move source decoding, target references and unsupported intent to their own observations. Compare whole-file writers across APIs without creating language or backend children.
micro-behaviors/fs/write/file/full.counterexample: A file handle is compatible with both append and overwrite; a Base64 decoder beside a writer does not establish the bytes written.
micro-behaviors/fs/write/file/full.status: parent review complete; per-rule destination map pending

micro-behaviors/os/user/account.question: Which user-account operation or reference is required?
micro-behaviors/os/user/account.parent_problem: The account resource restates much of os/user, while siblings already classify lookup, modify and delete operations. Its rules mix username words, account creation, password setting and shell configuration.
micro-behaviors/os/user/account.disposition: Review the complete os/user population by operation, separating user/account references from creation, lookup, modification and deletion. Decide the parent contract before migrating the broad account leaf; preserve unrelated group-membership and authority claims separately.
micro-behaviors/os/user/account.counterexample: The word username is a reference, not an account lookup; a dscl user creation and a password update are different operations.
micro-behaviors/os/user/account.status: parent review complete; per-rule destination map pending

sparse_review.criterion: Every former waiver is visible. For each cohort, compare the parent and peers; retain distinct claims while choosing a shallower representation where a child directory adds no necessary distinction. Count pressure alone does not authorize merging different claims.

migration_acceptance: Every old definition maps to one canonical destination, a proven equivalent, or a separately justified detection correction.
Every parent has one child question, with admission, exclusions and precedence.
Broad alternatives have an honest home without invented specificity.
Effective matching scope is preserved for moves.
Explicit references, directory selectors, exclusions and emitted schemas are reviewed together.
Each affected leaf has positive and near-miss validation fixtures.
Strict make validate passes after the hierarchy migration.
